methodology: Articles sourced from Virginia-specific RSS feeds and Google News RSS, filtered for AI/technology/workforce relevance, then assessed by Claude against the scenario framework. Each article is tagged with the region it most affects and the scenario it signals toward.

signals.title: Norfolk native brings free AI workshops to Hampton Roads to close the technology gap - WTKR
signals.signal_reading: Free AI workshops targeting Hampton Roads communities signal grassroots capability building outside traditional tech hubs, demonstrating distributed peer-to-peer knowledge transfer that could counter metro concentration if sustained and scaled.

signals.title: Roanoke College launches WorkAI Lab to prepare leaders for new era of technology - Roanoke College
signals.signal_reading: Roanoke College's WorkAI Lab represents institutional AI capacity building in a smaller market, but as a single academic initiative it signals isolated capability development rather than broad regional distribution without community-wide adoption mechanisms.

signals.title: New partnership between VCU and AI Ready RVA aims to boost AI education, innovation and community impact - VCU News
signals.signal_reading: VCU's partnership with AI Ready RVA explicitly targets community-wide AI education and innovation, signaling an intentional strategy to build distributed deep capability across Richmond's ecosystem beyond elite institutions alone.

signals.title: TAYLOR: AI data centers increase Virginia’s urban-rural divide - The Cavalier Daily
signals.signal_reading: Editorial analysis highlighting how data center concentration in NoVA's Loudoun County versus rural rejection elsewhere crystallizes the infrastructure divide that could prevent rural regions from accessing AI capabilities even as metro areas deepen theirs.

signals.title: Norfolk businesses are being urged not to miss out on the benefits of artificial intelligence - Rayo
signals.signal_reading: Urging Norfolk businesses to adopt AI suggests platform-driven shallow deployment where companies consume AI tools without building underlying technical capability, potentially creating broad but surface-level distribution dependent on vendor ecosystems.
